0.0.n: Literally triangle, this is the shop’s name here.

0.1.n: 屋 added to ケーキ identifies a shop selling cakes.

0.2.n: Usually attached to people’s names, さん also adds a friendly, respectful tone to shop names.

0.3.n: Placed after the shop name, 前 identifies the location outside it.

0.4.n: This polite ending completes a brief announcement with the subject left unstated.

1.0.n: The て-form of 待つ works as a direct request here.

1.2.n: The polite form of 乗る announces the speaker’s intention to board.

2.0.n: 三角 comes before ケーキ to describe its shape without an extra connecting word.

2.1.n: Japanese nouns do not mark singular or plural; the object particle を is omitted here.

2.2.n: This is the plain past form of 買う, placed before explanatory んです.

2.3.n: Short for の, this adds an explanatory tone as the speaker checks what they have noticed.

2.4.n: After ん, です makes the confirmation polite.

2.5.n: The ending ね invites the listener to confirm the speaker’s understanding.

3.0.n: そう refers back to the other speaker’s observation and agrees with it.

3.1.n: な connects そう to explanatory ん; it is part of the pattern そうなんです.

3.2.n: Short for の, this presents the reply as confirmation with an explanatory tone.

3.3.n: です finishes the confirmation politely.

3.5.n: 三角 directly describes the shape of the cakes.

3.6.n: The object particle を is left out after ケーキ in this casual speech.

3.8.n: いっぱい describes how much the speaker bought and sounds conversational.

3.9.n: Polite past of 買っちゃう, shortened from 買ってしまう, adds a playful sense of having gone ahead and bought them.

3.10.n: The ending よ emphasizes information the speaker is sharing with the listener.

4.0.n: そんなに points back to the quantity just mentioned and expresses surprise here.

0.lit: Triangle cake shop, in front, is.
0.tip: Shop name + 前です announces a location in front of the shop; arriving is understood from context.

1.tip: A て-form on its own can make a request, as 待って does here.

2.lit: Triangle cakes, bought—it’s that, isn’t it?
2.tip: んですね checks or acknowledges something the speaker has noticed.

3.lit: That’s how it is. Triangle cakes, lots, I ended up buying, you know!
3.tip: ちゃいました is a conversational shortening of てしまいました, here suggesting the speaker cheerfully bought more than expected.

4.tip: そんなに can stand alone as a surprised reaction to a quantity.
